The paper states H0/H1 and evaluates detectors at a 1% FPR operating point, so a reader could treat FPR 1% as the stated level. But what it reports on each comparison is a classifier's AUC at FPR 1% (and, in the in-the-wild audit, mean scores set against reference bands). It reports no confidence interval, p-value or test decision on the compared quantity, so I coded E4 false. On E3, the null pool is the same checkpoint and configuration on H200/A100, TP-1/TP-4 and vLLM/HF. On E5, the Token-DiFR margin and the cross-entropy baseline come from the reference's teacher-forced logits on the provider's claimed tokens; the served side contributes only sampled tokens. On E6, code is released at github.com/adamkarvonen/difr, but the text gives no prompt-set digest.

verdicts.object: A served LLM API endpoint's first-token top-k logprob distribution on a fixed one-token prompt, compared against the same endpoint at an earlier time (189 endpoints monitored hourly). In vitro, an open-weight model is compared against its own fine-tuned, LoRA, pruned or noised variants (TinyChange), using an original/original null distribution.
verdicts.reason: E1, E2, E3 and E5 are done for this object. E3: 1,000 original/original tests on identical weights, run in the batched vLLM setup, give the null distribution the ROC/AUC verdict rests on. E4 is not done. The permutation test is defined against a symbolic significance level alpha that is never set, and no p-values are reported. The 95% CIs are on detector AUC, not on the compared quantity. Real-world flags use a 12-standard-deviation threshold with no stated level. Distance 1, missing E4. E6 not done: the prompt 'x' and the code are public, with no digest.

sources.notes: Chauvin, Le Merrer, Taiani, Tredan, arXiv 2512.03816v2. This is the nearest C4a neighbour in my set: E1, E2, E3 and E5 are carried for one object, so its distance is 1 and the missing element is E4. E4 is the element a second reader is most likely to code differently. Arguments for true: a permutation test is defined whose null is 'identical distributions', and 95% CIs are reported. Why I coded false: alpha is never given a value, no p-value is reported for any comparison, and the CIs bound AUC rather than the compared statistic S. E3 is carried only by the in-vitro TinyChange runs, where identical weights are known. The real-world endpoint threshold uses historical variance of an endpoint whose identity is only inferred, which does not count as E3 under the protocol.

verdicts.object: ERROR (Elson, Hussey, Arslan; University of Bern), a standing bug-bounty programme of at least four years. It pays specialist reviewers a base rate plus an error-size bonus for checking highly cited published papers, with author consent.

verdicts.object: A SHA-256 hash chain over canonical-JSON stage spec records of a hybrid quantum-classical pipeline, anchored to an append-only external log. Replay recomputes every hash (verify_full_chain, verify_against_anchor).
verdicts.reason: It does a tamper-evident chained log with replay verification and external anchoring. What is chained is stage parameter/spec records, which may include observable contracts. It does not chain verdicts re-derived from bytes: observable-deviation verdicts are raised as exceptions at commit time and are not recomputed on replay, and replay re-derives only the hash links.

verdicts.object: A quantum stage (single-qubit circuit channel) compared against a contract supertype's Pauli expectation values on six fixed input states, within a tolerance epsilon calibrated from repeated noisy runs of a valid override. Also cloud QPU auditing of a claimed backend.
verdicts.reason: Only E2 is done: six input states are fixed and applied to candidate and supertype. The object is a quantum circuit or hardware backend, not a model or weights, so E1 fails. The epsilon floor from the 95th percentile of repeated Bgood runs is a structural analogue of E3 on a non-model object and has no identical weights. The threshold carries no stated test level (E4 not done). The compared quantity is Pauli expectations from shot counts, not token log-probabilities (E5 not done). No digest of inputs is published (E6 not done).

sources.notes: Yeniaras and Karimov, arXiv 2605.13109v1, 13 May 2026. The last non-empty line of the extracted text is the page number '30'. C2 is OCCUPIED by a hash-chained spec log with replay and anchor, not a chain of re-derived verdicts. For C4a, the tolerance-calibration procedure (repeated runs of a known-valid override, 95th percentile, threshold set just above it) is structurally E3-like, but it is applied to quantum channels, not model weights, so I coded it false under the protocol's wording.
